items.title: A delivery gap at Armenia and Pereira traced to our own fetch script, not to the ingest
items.summary: Collects over those two cities could never reach Carya: the fetch tool built its work list by scanning a staging tree that holds five of the seven cities. Both are active targets and both download normally everywhere else, so waiting would never have helped. The tool now accepts an explicit work list taken from the tasking API and depends on no local tree.

items.title: Field returns from QField checked building by building: duplicates, locations, footprints
items.summary: Riccardo Vitale consolidated the survey teams' QField GeoPackages into one dataset, removed duplicate records, corrected each building's position against the facade photographs, digitised a footprint for every building and flagged the locations that remain uncertain. items.title: All 248 Colombia Umbra collects regenerated at native posting under the group standard
items.summary: The 24 September geocoding oversampled 1 m products to 0.31 m, 3.3 times, and was discarded. Umbra 1 m products post at 0.903 m, 0.25 m products at 0.226 m.

items.title: Coherence_Maps bug fixed: IW2 and IW3 bursts were geocoded one subswath east
items.summary: ASF burst annotation XML concatenates all three subswaths and four readers always took the IW1 block. New annotation.py selects the block matching the swath in the file name. Cali (303914, 303915) and Quibdó (303901, 303902) bursts reprocessed; IW1 results for Pereira, Armenia, Manizales, Quimbaya and Sevilla unaffected.

items.title: Geoid fix: Copernicus GLO-30 orthometric heights caused a 40 m eastward shift in geocoded coherence
items.summary: Footprint-shift test on Pereira 303906 and Armenia 303908 peaks at +40 m east, -5 m north. EGM2008 undulation (26.6 to 27.8 m) at 34 degrees incidence predicts 39 to 42 m. download_cop30_dem now adds the undulation (mean 26.29 m over Pereira). Current 20 m products keep the 2-pixel offset; city statistics unaffected.

items.title: USGS Key Points and Tectonic Summary: 10.5 million people exposed to MMI VI to VII, intraslab strike-slip
items.summary: Reviewed USGS general-text product (Key Points dated 10 Aug 22:23 UTC, product updated 11 Aug 21:14 UTC). About 10.5 million people experienced Strong (MMI VI) to Very Strong (MMI VII) shaking and USGS assesses a high likelihood of widespread damage and casualties. The event is described as primarily strike-slip faulting at about 110 km depth within the subducting Nazca plate, near the northern limit of intermediate-depth seismicity in the South America subduction zone. Since 1950 two earthquakes of M7 or larger occurred within 250 km, both near the coast; the 1999 M6.1 Armenia crustal earthquake caused over 1,000 fatalities and destroyed around 50 percent of the houses in Pereira.
